newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds Metals sees aluminum can growth.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds Metals sees aluminum can growth.

text.p: The U.S. beverage can market should expand by two percent a year, while soft drink can markets in developing countries will see double-digit growth annually, Jeremiah Sheehan, chief executive of Reynolds Metals Co, said Wednesday.
"We expect the U.S. beverage can market to continue to grow about two percent annually," Sheehan said.
Speaking at the Aluminum Association's Alumitech 1997 conference here, Sheehan said aluminum cans increased their share of the U.S. soft drink packaging mix in 1996.
The U.S. market accounted for 63 billion cans sold for soft drinks last year, compared with 18 billion PET (plastic) containers and fewer than two billion glass containers.
"PET growth has been at the expense of glass, primarily in single service packages sold in convenience stores where consumers seem to be much more willing to pay a premium," he said.
Sheehan said PET growth had not taken hold in grocery stores or in vending machines, where aluminum cans hold the lion's share in soft drink packaging market.

In a reference to the automotive market, the Reynolds executive also predicted the aluminum content of North American-made cars would rise to 410 lbs per vehicle by 2006 and to 950 lbs by 2020 from 252 lbs in 1996.
